ucgs_block_i.rule: Complete both courses for six credits.

ucgs_block_ii.rule: Choose two three-credit courses from different categories.

ucgs_block_v.rule: Choose one mathematics course; the heading prints 3-4 credits while MTH 167 is listed at five credits.

ucgs_block_vii.rule: Choose two courses totaling 6-8 credits, aligned with the intended transfer destination.
ucgs_block_vii.eligible_courses: Any course in UCGS Blocks I-VI, any approved course on the statewide combined Passport/UCGS roster, plus the locally listed additions below.
ucgs_block_vii.foreign_language_placeholder_rule: The source also prints generic foreign-language levels 101, 102, 201, and 202 rather than a concrete language prefix.

science_specialized.rule: Complete 12 credits from the locally listed menu or other courses identified in the Transfer Virginia common curriculum for Computer Science or another STEM destination.

transfer_core.rule: Complete 16-18 credits of transfer-intended courses aligned to the receiving program and Transfer Virginia common curriculum.

unit_audit.closure_basis: 1 + 31 + 12 + 16 = 60 on the canonical minimum path; the published UCGS and Transfer Core component maxima close the published degree maximum at 1 + 33 + 12 + 18 = 64.

residency.rule: Twenty-five percent of the degree credits, excluding advanced-placement and credit-by-exam credit, must be acquired at Mountain Gateway Community College.

modeling_notes: This is the current generic Science A.S., not a standalone Computer Science award. It belongs in scope because both the degree catalog and college program page expressly name Computer Science as a supported Transfer Virginia pathway.
No CS-specific CSC sequence is prescribed. Science Specialized and Transfer Core selections remain receiving-program-dependent rather than being replaced with a speculative schedule.
The program's Biology and Natural Resources guided-pathway rows are excluded because they are destination-specific maps, not universal degree requirements and not Computer Science maps.
Concrete locally listed course menus remain on the API object in option_sets even where the source's choose-by-credit/open-roster rule cannot be reduced to an ordinary choose-N receiver.

data_quality_flags.message: The award supports Computer Science transfer, but Mountain Gateway publishes no CS-specific prescribed course branch.
The 12-credit Science Specialized and 16-18-credit Transfer Core components depend on the receiving curriculum and can include approved courses outside the locally listed menus.

The UCGS publishes a 31-33 component total, while its locally listed five-credit MTH 167 and 6-8 credit Block VII routes can arithmetically exceed 33; the degree's published component cap is retained.
